note: The product's recorded Core Web Vitals, per route, per emulated device, per cache temperature, plus the four product timings the 2026-09-05 audit's R2 named. perf/route-budgets.json holds what a route COSTS; this holds what a person FEELS. Read docs/perf/baseline-2026-09-05.md before changing a number: down is free, and up needs a sentence in `debt` saying what got slower and why. lib/webVitalsBaseline.ts owns the rules; e2e/cwv-baseline.spec.ts is the only writer, under `npm run perf:cwv-record`, and the same spec under `npm run perf:cwv-sweep` is the fence, spent by hand before a merge because no CI job runs it. A figure over its R2 target (LCP 2500 ms, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1) is DEBT and must carry its reason: __tests__/webVitalsBaseline.test.ts fails on an unowned one.

method.build: local production build (NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-prod), keyless, served by next start; Playwright Chromium with SwiftShader so the map gets a real WebGL2 context and the sweep measures the map rather than its fallback. Taken on a shared box at load average ~52 on 18 cores, so these are pessimistic ceilings rather than clean figures. The desktop arm was taken on 2026-09-06 against a local production build on a private port, three runs a cell, on the same shared box.
method.inpNote: INP is the worst interaction the run produced, read off Event Timing entries carrying an interactionId. The API's durationThreshold floors at 16 ms, so a route whose interaction finished inside one frame reports no entry and is recorded at 16 rather than at 0: we did not see it, which is not the same as it taking no time.
method.coverage: Mobile and desktop, 3 runs per cell, median. The MOBILE half is the whole route list, recorded 2026-09-05 at commit 9b6dbcd8c from one sweep of the shipped tree (docs/proof/perf-baseline-fix/sweep-after-arm.log). The DESKTOP half is narrower and says so: `/`, `/map` and `/pal`, the three routes Astra's 6 September audit named, recorded 2026-09-06. Desktop is not the full list because one run of both full lists does not finish inside the spec's own timeout, which is why the desktop `/map` warm cell had never completed here before; the recorder now re-takes one device without discarding the other, so each half is a run of its own. `/pal` is a desktop row alone: the mobile table predates the route and a device's rows are only ever re-taken by a run of that device. Every figure here was printed by a run; none was typed.

Taken on a shared box whose per-sample spread reached 6.5x on this cell (warm samples 648/4184/4128 ms), so this is a pessimistic ceiling rather than a clean figure. Recorded so it cannot regress unnoticed.
